build_provenance.validation: This build-time checkpoint adds a16MiB manifest input cap and rejects unknown scope/status. Runtime tests, actual focused acquisition and analysis comparisons are recorded externally.

durability_contract: Success exit requires payload, ledger, manifest and output/parent directory fsync; stderr/exit status is authoritative on final publication failure.

filter.exclusion_basis: LRU, BUDDY, MMAP, ANON, SWAPCACHE, SWAPBACKED, KSM, THP and ZERO_PAGE are excluded unless SLAB/PGTABLE is set. Unsafe flags always exclude.
filter.retained: SLAB, PGTABLE and unclassified pages are retained. The sole boundary exception is an immediate SLAB neighbor with BUDDY and no other exclusion bit. It never reintroduces user/cache classified pages. Free residual bytes may remain; no exact kernel-only guarantee.

limitations: Non-atomic live acquisition: flags, addresses and payload are observed at different times.
Kernel-focused filtering can omit kernel-relevant information and retain user/residual bytes.
kcore can return internally zero-filled bytes; read success is not proof of physical-byte availability.
Unsafe/unmapped PFNs are explicit omissions and prevent complete status.
Cancellation is cooperative; a kernel I/O syscall can block beyond the request.
Payload budget excludes metadata, allocator overhead and OS page cache.
Matching symbols and successful plugins do not prove complete forensic coverage.

source_io.semantics: Successful pread return bytes, including partial reads before error; not filesystem or physical disk traffic. Metadata files other than kcore/kpageflags are excluded.

io_at_probe.semantics: Successful pread return bytes, including partial reads before error; not filesystem or physical disk traffic. Metadata files other than kcore/kpageflags are excluded.
